draft.title: Working conditions and child labour
card: In early industrial Britain, many factory and mine workers worked 12 to 16 hours a day, six days a week. Wages were low, and workers who complained could lose their jobs.
Work was dangerous. Machines had no safety guards, and fingers and limbs were often caught. Mines had cave-ins and explosions, and cotton mills were hot, noisy and full of dust.
Children worked too, some from the age of five or six. Owners paid them less than adults, and small children could fit into places adults could not, such as under machines or in narrow mine tunnels.
Many poor families needed every wage to pay for food and rent, so they sent their children to work. Children who were tired or slow could be beaten.
draft.remember: Long hours, low pay and danger were normal for industrial workers, and poor families relied on children's wages.

a.q: Why did many poor families send young children to work in factories and mines?
opts: The family needed every wage to pay for food and rent
Children were paid more than adults for the same work
Children were the only people who could run the machines
The law required every child over five to work in a mill
a.why: Wages were low, so poor families needed all the money they could earn. Children were paid less than adults, not more, which is why owners liked to hire them.
a.clue: Think about what a poor family had to pay for each week.

b.q: In 1830, a mill owner in Lancashire hires many young children and few adults. Using what you know about industrial work, what is the most likely reason?
opts: Children cost less to employ and could fit near machines
Children worked faster and longer hours than adult workers
Children were safer around machines than adults were
Children were better educated and so easier to train
b.why: Owners paid children less than adults, and small children could reach tight spaces near machines. It is tempting to think children were safer, but machines had no guards and children were often hurt.
b.clue: Think about what owners paid, and about the size of a small child.

a.best: The family needed every wage to pay for food and rent

b.best: Children cost less to employ and could fit near machines

problems.detail: The clue ('what owners paid, and about the size of a small child') restates both halves of the right option, so a student can match the clue to the answer without recalling the idea.

check.summary: The facts and answers are sound. The only issue is that question b's clue points so directly at the right option that it nearly gives the answer away. Child labour and the beating of children are flagged as sensitive for awareness.

flags: Question b, other: The clue ('what owners paid, and about the size of a small child') restates both halves of the right option, so a student can match the clue to the answer without recalling the idea.
